chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sells to the people on credit (with deferred payment) and his own wealth is the guarantee, so he said: 'If his soul is pleased with that, I only dislike it because I fear they will charge him more than what he gains from them. But if his soul is pleased with that, there is no harm.'

key_terms.ضَمَانُ مَالِهِمْ: Guarantee of their wealth (seller bears risk)
key_terms.يُغَرِّمُوهُ: They will charge him/hold him liable

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods on credit when the seller guarantees the payment?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic distinction between personal preference (*karahat*) and legal permissibility (*ibahah*) in commercial contracts. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that bearing the risk of buyer default is valid provided the seller consents, reflecting the principle of *taysir* (ease) in transactions. This ruling underscores the importance of mutual consent and risk allocation in Islamic finance, distinguishing between moral caution and binding legal validity.
